steps.label: Test and Debug
steps.content:
Year 6 Scratch

Test and Debug

Year 6, 6.2.6

  • Test a program like a tester: expected against actual.
  • Find and fix the bugs in six broken games.
  • Test a partner's game and record what you find.

steps.label: Test It Like a Tester
steps.content:
Test It Like a Tester

A bug is where what should happen and what does happen are different.

Think → Pair → ShareClicked 9 times: expected no message, and there was no message. Is that a bug? Why test it at all?Show the answer

No, expected and actual match. You test 9 to prove the message does not come too early: bugs often hide just below or above a target.

I didExpectedActual
Held left arrowShip moves leftIt moved right
Clicked 10 timesSays You win!Said nothing
Clicked 9 timesNo message yetNo message
  • Test every control, one at a time.
  • Test the edges: the sides of the stage, the floor.
  • Test either side of a target: 9, 10 and 11 clicks.
  • Change one thing, then test again.

steps.label: Check: Testing
steps.content:
Check: Testing

Choose the best answer.

items.prompt: A game should say You win! at 10 clicks. Which click counts should you test?
items.explain: Test just below, on, and just above the target. Off-by-one bugs hide there.

items.prompt: Expected: the Ship moves left. Actual: it moves right. What is this?
items.explain: Expected and actual are different, so there is a bug to fix.

steps.label: Activity 1: Bug Hunt 1 to 3
steps.content:
Activity 1: Bug Hunt 1 to 3

Work on your own. Each game has one bug. Play it, find the bug, fix it, then press Next.

Build it

  • Bug Hunt 1: Meteor Dodge. One control is broken.
  • Bug Hunt 2: Meteor Dodge never ends.
  • Bug Hunt 3: Balloon Pop. The score gets stuck.
  • Play first: watch what happens before you change any blocks.

The panel beside TurboWarp lists the checks. Press Check my project as often as you like: it plays your game and tells you what it saw.

steps.label: Where Bugs Hide
steps.content:
Where Bugs Hide

What you see tells you where to look.

Think → Pair → ShareThe time box goes 20, 21, 22. Which kind of bug is that? Where do you look?Show the answer

It goes the wrong way. Look at the change [time] by block: the number should be -1, not 1.

Goes the wrong wayLook at the numbers in the move and change blocks. Is one positive when it should be negative?
Happens once, then stopsBlocks that should keep running need to be inside a forever or repeat loop.
A value gets stuckRead the blocks that change it. Does it say set when it should say change?
Something never happensRead the condition. Which sprite does it check? Can the comparison ever be true?

steps.label: Test a Partner's Game
steps.content:
Test a Partner's Game

Swap with a partner and play their game from 6.2.5. Fill in one row for each test.

Think → Pair → ShareYour partner reads "it does not work". Can they fix it? What would help them more?Show the answer

No: they do not know what you did or what went wrong. "Held the up arrow at the top edge. Expected: stop. Actual: went off the stage" tells them exactly where to look.

I didExpectedActual

Show your partner each row where expected and actual are different.

steps.label: Checked Practice
steps.content:
Checked Practice

Use what you found in the Bug Hunts.

items.prompt: score should go up by 1 per coin, but it jumps by 3 every time. Where do you look first?
items.explain: The script that changes score is the one that runs too many times: often because the Coin stays touching and nothing moves it away.

items.prompt: A game should end when lives reaches 0, but it never ends. Which condition has a bug?
items.explain: lives stops at 0, so "less than 0" is never true. It should be "= 0".
